stop_condition: Every one of round 1's nine findings is verified fixed against the code and the clone's store rather than against the author's description of the fix; and no NEW contradiction was introduced by the nine edits, judged by reading each changed region contiguously as rendered. No critical/high finding remains in the release-surface claims (CHANGELOG, README) or the v5.0.0 ledger rows.

findings.evidence: The R1-F4 fix names the second untrustworthy check as "the coherence rollup that consumes it (`qa-gate.sh` runs `design-conform` as LEG 1's subprocess, so the rollup inherits whatever the conformance check saw)". The rollup does the OPPOSITE. `cmd_approve` runs TWO separate refusals: DESIGN-ALIGNMENT-REFUSAL calls `compute_design_alignment "$tid"` in DEFAULT mode (qa-gate.sh:7305) and that path DOES shell out to design-conform (:15184, inside the `LEG-1-FILES-ROLLUP-SKIP` sentinel region); COHERENCE-ROLLUP-REFUSAL calls `compute_design_coherence "$tid"` (:7357), which calls `compute_design_alignment "$cid" "rollup"` (:15963), and the leg is guarded by `if [ "$mode" != "rollup" ]; then` (:15182) -- so LEG 1 never runs for the rollup. The function's own header says it in so many words: "mode=rollup SKIPS LEG 1 (files) entirely and starts at LEG 2" and "Condition 2 of D6 (scope drift ...) is computed separately, in compute_design_coherence itself, from the SAME durable completion-payload evidence LEG 3 already establishes how to read -- not from this skipped leg" (:15119-15145). Mechanically: `awk 'NR>=15663 && NR<=16294 { line=$0; sub(/^[ \t]+/,"",line); if (line !~ /^#/ && $0 ~ /design-conform/) print NR }' .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh` at 897b7fe returns NOTHING -- zero non-comment references to design-conform anywhere in compute_design_coherence's body.
findings.description: A false mechanism claim about shipped code, on the primary release surface, inside the paragraph that justifies the release's headline decision (shipping the design phase opt-in) -- and it is refuted by a comment block in the code that states the opposite in plain words. The COUNT ("two checks") and the CONCLUSION (the rollup is also untrustworthy on an empty change set) both survive; only the stated route is wrong. The rollup reaches the same exposure by its OWN tracker read, not by inheriting design-conform's: `live_diff_raw=$(bash "$IMPACT_REPORT_SCRIPT" --relativized-changed-files ...)` at :16119, whose under-coverage direction ("diff MINUS rollup") is the gating one -- an empty tracker yields an empty diff set, so that gate can never fire. Two correct fixes, either acceptable: (a) name `design-unit-align` / DESIGN-ALIGNMENT-REFUSAL as the second check, which genuinely does run design-conform as LEG 1's subprocess; or (b) keep the rollup and state its real route (its own `impact-report.sh --relativized-changed-files` read, with LEG 1 explicitly skipped for the documented correctness reason). Do NOT keep the current wording: the skip is deliberate, sentinel-guarded and load-bearing, and a release note asserting the opposite will be read as the specification of behaviour the code does not have.

findings.evidence: R1-F5's location field named "CHANGELOG.md:41-48 and README.md:186-190". Only the CHANGELOG half was fixed. README.md:187 at the current tree still reads "**5 minutes** for a small code change and **19 minutes** for a doc-only one, both approved in one round" (`grep -n '5 minutes' README.md` -> 187). The CHANGELOG, in the SAME uncommitted change set, now retracts exactly those two numbers in terms: "*(An earlier draft said \"5 minutes\" and \"19 minutes\" with no anchor; neither reproduced at any anchor ...)*" (CHANGELOG.md:48-50), and replaces them with 3m57s / 17m51s. I re-derived both from the F4 clone's own store at /var/folders/qr/c0gwdny174v7dbphnj1l7wy40000gn/T/cwpf4.XXXXXX.1Eqtm8TbLC/proj via `bd show <id> --json --include-comments`: target-2c5 enter 2026-09-29T15:14:07Z -> QA-GATE APPROVED 15:18:04Z = 3m57s; target-w8v enter 14:51:19Z -> approved 15:09:10Z = 17m51s. Neither is 5 nor 19 minutes at that anchor, and target-w8v cannot be rescued by a creation anchor either (created 2026-09-28T17:35:14Z, approved 21h later).
findings.description: The most-read release surface publishes two numbers that its sibling surface, in the same change set, states did not reproduce. This is not merely an unanchored figure: it is a figure the project has itself now recorded as unreproducible, left standing as a measurement. The same ledger carries row Q2, where an unmeasured "in 5 minutes" claim was DROPPED under prove-or-remove (docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:162) -- README now republishes a "5 minutes" that has been through the same disproof. Fix: mirror the CHANGELOG's corrected pair and its anchor into README, or drop the two default-path figures from README and point at the CHANGELOG. Note CONTRIBUTING.md:571-573 enumerates RELEASE_AUDIT rows, CHANGELOG entries, HANDOFF verify blocks, task closures and review artifacts -- README is not in that list, so the rule does not formally bind it; the finding does not rest on that rule, it rests on the number being known-wrong.

findings.evidence: The fixed paragraph states one anchor for the default pair -- "both measured gate-`enter` to change-set-bound approval, from the F4 clone's own Beads store (`bd show <id> --json --include-comments`: ...)" -- and then, in the next sentence, gives "**3 hours 24 minutes**" and a "**49,512-byte**" artifact with no command, no commit and no anchor. Both reproduce, but on a DIFFERENT anchor than the one just stated: target-23z created 2026-09-28T16:03:55Z -> last same-day COMPLETION v1 on target-23z.1 at 2026-09-28T19:27:38Z = 3h23m43s (creation -> last completion). Under the anchor the sentence actually names, the design path was 15:41:15Z -> 15:53:25Z = 12m10s. `wc -c <clone>/flagship/docs/specs/target-23z.md` -> 49512 confirms the byte figure.
findings.description: R1-F5's evidence was "These four carry neither"; two of the four are now anchored and two are not, and the two that are not sit in the same comparison as the two that are. A reader takes "3m57s default versus 3h24m design" as a like-for-like ratio; it is not, and nothing in the text says so. This is the exact failure CONTRIBUTING.md:576-585 names -- several counts of nominally the same quantity, no two stating their method, so no two comparable. The 3h24m figure is the HONEST cost number (the design work precedes gate-enter, so the gate-anchored 12m10s would understate it); the defect is that the difference is silent. Fix: state the design-path anchor explicitly ("design-task creation to the last same-day COMPLETION v1 on its unit") and give the command for both it and the byte count, as the sentence above already does for the pair.

findings.evidence: The tally-note edit changed "That figure moved TWICE on 2026-09-29" to "That figure moved THREE TIMES on 2026-09-29" but left the date qualifier untouched, while the newly-added third move is dated two clauses later: "then on 2026-09-30 `DP4` was scoped to F4's evidence" (:851-854). Of the three enumerated transitions (11/6/0/1 -> 10/6/1/1 -> 10/7/0/1 -> 9/8/0/1), two are on 2026-09-29 and one is on 2026-09-30.
findings.description: The TWICE -> THREE TIMES half of the edit landed; the "on 2026-09-29" half did not. Self-correcting within the same sentence, so no reader is misled about when DP4 moved -- but this ledger's subject matter is precisely counts stated without their scope, and its own movement record should not carry one. Fix: "moved TWICE on 2026-09-29 and once more on 2026-09-30", or "moved THREE TIMES across 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-30".

findings.evidence: The new DP5 correction cites "`grep -c isolation .claude/agents/*.md` finds no frontmatter declaration". Run at 897b7fe that command returns per-file COUNTS, several nonzero: designer 0, judge 0, design-reviewer 0, grader 0, backend 1, devops 0, qa 2, orchestrator 8, frontend 0. It cannot establish WHERE a token appears, so it cannot establish the stated conclusion. The conclusion is nonetheless TRUE -- extracting each file's YAML frontmatter (`awk 'NR==1 && $0=="---"{fm=1; next} fm && $0=="---"{exit} fm' <f> | grep isolation`) returns nothing for all nine agents; the nonzero hits are prose and code-block matches (orchestrator.md:417-434's own section, qa.md's unrelated prose, backend.md:42's "isolation level" in a database sentence). Every other claim in this correction verifies exactly: orchestrator.md:417 is "#### 4b. Worktree isolation for parallel specialists (spec 0.6)" with the worked Task examples and .worktreeinclude; docs/AGENTS.md:1172 is the matching section and :1177 carries the platform-docs citation; and `git show v4.1.0:.claude/agents/orchestrator.md | grep -c 'isolation: "worktree"'` -> 4, equal to HEAD -> 4.
findings.description: A command/conclusion mismatch in a row whose entire purpose this cycle was to state a claim precisely after getting it wrong in both directions. The fact is right; the cited evidence does not produce it, so a reader re-running the command gets nine counts and no answer. Fix: cite the frontmatter-scoped command, or state the conclusion as "no agent's YAML frontmatter declares it; the only occurrences are prose".

findings.evidence: The CHANGELOG's opt-in rationale says "`design-conform` has been observed exactly once on a real repository and the observation was VACUOUS". DP4, edited in the same change set, says the empty-change-set conform "happened twice, by two independent routes: first on a path whose ancestor directory name collided with the shared denylist (`claude-workflow-plugin-pqoj`), then again on a denylist-clean path via a cross-session gate-baseline swallow (`claude-workflow-plugin-q5l6`)". The residual bullet added at :984-997 carries both framings in adjacent sentences: "Observed exactly once on a real product repository ... Two independent routes reached it". The task's own SPEC contains the same pair ("observed exactly once on a real target" in the WHY OPT-IN paragraph; "vacuous in a target, twice, by two independent routes" in the DP4 paragraph), so the change set reproduces the SPEC faithfully rather than introducing the tension.
findings.description: Reconcilable under one reading -- design-conform was RUN on a real target once, while the empty-change-set CONDITION was reached twice, only one of those on the real target (pqoj is a target-path denylist collision; q5l6 is titled for the tracker-empty-at-first-enter case and is an open task on this repo). But the text never says which noun each count attaches to, and the quantity in question is exactly how much evidence stands behind the release's headline caveat. Fix: make the nouns explicit in both places -- e.g. "one observation of `design-conform` on a real target; the empty-change-set input condition reached twice, by two independent routes".

findings.evidence: (a) R1-F4 noted the two release surfaces disagreed on how many checks are untrustworthy. The CHANGELOG now names two; README.md:183-184 still names one ("the design phase's conformance check is not something to rely on"). README makes no count claim, so it is incomplete rather than false. (b) The R1-F6 supersession block leaves two consecutive blank lines at docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1279-1280 before "Recorded because a row can be right..." -- the same cosmetic class as R1-F9, which WAS fixed in README (the seam there is now a single blank line).
findings.description: Both non-blocking. Worth clearing while the files are open, particularly (a): once R2-F1 is resolved the second check will have a correct name, and README is the surface an operator reads first when deciding whether to opt in.
